bets.title: One executable semantic core supports proof-first development
bets.hypothesis: A dependency-light kernel can share production, const-evaluated, Kani-checked and Verus-verified executable semantics at acceptable proof/build cost.
bets.success_witness: The cardinality kernel and external identity consumer succeed in every declared profile, with matched executable/specification identity and a recorded target-aware contract.
bets.negative_control: Multiply before noticing a zero extent; remove a constructor invariant; suppress a failed harness. Each must fail its intended gate.
bets.falsifier: The selected language/toolchain subset needs an unproved substitute executable body, a trusted whole-executor axiom, or proof costs above pre-registered limits.
bets.decision_rule: Revise the kernel representation or narrow the certified subset before stabilization; do not abandon the proof-first requirement or hide a duplicate checker.
bets.measurement: Record workload, compiler/verifier/backend revisions, target/features, assumptions, and cost against the pre-registered acceptance controls (spec/acceptance-controls.json). Correctness gates are categorical; empirical thresholds are the registered controls.

bets.title: Consumers compose application proofs through the public API
bets.hypothesis: Logical views, typed checked inputs, and higher-order contracts let separate consumer crates verify useful programmes without internal imports or new notation.
bets.success_witness: Kani and Verus consumers establish round-trip and selection properties through comb!, custom kernels and reducers, including success and failure witnesses with exact scopes.
bets.negative_control: Wrong transpose result, always-Err executor, stale source witness, or an assumed executor postcondition must not pass.
bets.falsifier: A consumer must unfold private executor code, import private symbols, change executable routes under proof cfg, or assume the very property being claimed.
bets.decision_rule: Revise public contracts/views and preserve production bindings before stabilizing them; record unsupported advanced properties explicitly.
bets.measurement: Record workload, compiler/verifier/backend revisions, target/features, assumptions, and cost against the pre-registered acceptance controls (spec/acceptance-controls.json). Correctness gates are categorical; empirical thresholds are the registered controls.

bets.title: Compile-time admission is useful without type-level shape machinery
bets.hypothesis: Static or bounded descriptors can discharge useful resource obligations through the same restricted analyser used during preparation and execution.
bets.success_witness: Exact 4096^2 non-null F64 materialization rejects 64 MiB; bounded inputs distinguish uncertifiable domain from certain excess; smaller exact inputs pass. Runtime and const checks agree on both target-width profiles.
bets.negative_control: Treat unknown as zero, treat an upper bound as a lower bound, use host usize layout, or execute a host configuration read during compilation.
bets.falsifier: The compiler accepts a known over-budget case, rejects all dynamic uses, reports false certainty, or needs unacceptable compile latency to certify the agreed examples.
bets.decision_rule: Reduce static expression/shape scope and retain explicit runtime admission; strict certification fails closed without changing comb! ergonomics.
bets.measurement: Record workload, compiler/verifier/backend revisions, target/features, assumptions, and cost against the pre-registered acceptance controls (spec/acceptance-controls.json). Correctness gates are categorical; empirical thresholds are the registered controls.

bets.title: A small checker can validate scoped resource and rewrite claims
bets.hypothesis: A planner can propose schedules while a smaller checked kernel validates shape, guard, liveness and resource obligations independently of planner heuristics.
bets.success_witness: Admitted native schedules respect distinct live backing capacities plus scratch/halos under declared kernel contracts; runtime reservations reject the first forbidden expansion.
bets.negative_control: Understate halo scratch, reuse a stale certificate, double-count one alias, omit a guard or permit untracked disk writes in a strict profile.
bets.falsifier: The checker admits a violating schedule, certifies choices the backend may replace with unbounded alternatives, or relies on an unvalidated kernel declaration as unconditional evidence.
bets.decision_rule: Restrict schedules/capabilities or require runtime checks; narrow certificates to tracked resources and list external assumptions instead of promising process RSS.
bets.measurement: Record workload, compiler/verifier/backend revisions, target/features, assumptions, and cost against the pre-registered acceptance controls (spec/acceptance-controls.json). Correctness gates are categorical; empirical thresholds are the registered controls.

bets.title: Streaming Polars preserves the positional and resource contract
bets.hypothesis: Explicit engine/order/spill policies can admit useful Polars 2-era regions while preserving correspondence, validity and bounded owned resources.
bets.success_witness: Pinned Rust engines pass forced-order/null/empty/chunk/halo cases; no-spill requirements are enforced or admission refuses the route. Opt-in spill exercises quota and cancellation cleanup.
bets.negative_control: Shuffle rows, lose a parent validity bit, split a segment, or apply a process-global policy as if it were independent per-query state.
bets.falsifier: A supported route changes positional meaning, performs undisclosed I/O, or reports a hard per-plan bound without an available control.
bets.decision_rule: Disable the capability or select a faithful explicitly permitted route; keep strict policy failures visible and do not infer support from Python versioning.
bets.measurement: Record workload, compiler/verifier/backend revisions, target/features, assumptions, and cost against the pre-registered acceptance controls (spec/acceptance-controls.json). Correctness gates are categorical; empirical thresholds are the registered controls.

bets.title: New upstream optimizer hooks produce measurable benefit without semantic leakage
bets.hypothesis: Dtype-aware planning, deterministic-plugin optimization and physical provenance can improve the adapter when the pinned Rust API exposes compatible capabilities.
bets.success_witness: A named workload compares capability-enabled and disabled routes under pre-registered criteria; results/failures match and source attribution survives. Unsupported hooks have explicit dispositions.
bets.negative_control: Use determinism alone to speculate a fallible branch, treat metadata as a valid Normal3, or claim planning-time specialization is Rust compile-time evaluation.
bets.falsifier: No supported interface exists, required equivalence fails, or measured benefit does not justify coupling and maintenance cost.
bets.decision_rule: Decline that optional hook while retaining the semantic port and first-class Polars baseline; capability availability is not a mandate to use it.
bets.measurement: Record workload, compiler/verifier/backend revisions, target/features, assumptions, and cost against the pre-registered acceptance controls (spec/acceptance-controls.json). Correctness gates are categorical; empirical thresholds are the registered controls.

bets.title: Typed and segmented consumers prove orchestration without replacing domain mathematics
bets.hypothesis: Public cell, mask, segment and reducer contracts let rendering-shaped consumers establish identity, active-only execution and atomic commit independently of their numeric kernels.
bets.success_witness: Both downstream toolchain fixtures establish correspondence, segment ownership, reducer history and pre-commit unchanged output with actual user kernels; geometry/scheduler assumptions remain separately listed.
bets.negative_control: Invoke a faulting inactive kernel, permute only normals, drop empty segments, merge float accumulators without permission, or commit a cancelled tile.
bets.falsifier: The proof requires inventing numerical correctness, assuming callback termination without disclosure, or silently replacing the concurrent/SIMD implementation by scalar code.
bets.decision_rule: Keep direct domain code and narrow the proven orchestration route; record continue/revise/decline for trasic separately from proof SDK acceptance.
bets.measurement: Record workload, compiler/verifier/backend revisions, target/features, assumptions, and cost against the pre-registered acceptance controls (spec/acceptance-controls.json). Correctness gates are categorical; empirical thresholds are the registered controls.

bets.title: Evidence and proof-API compatibility remain maintainable
bets.hypothesis: Versioned models, executable bindings and scoped proof records allow downstream proofs to survive legitimate internals changes and fail when their assumptions change.
bets.success_witness: An internal refactor preserves public proofs; precondition strengthening, postcondition weakening, backend/profile changes and stale specification bindings invalidate the affected evidence and cache entries.
bets.negative_control: Import verification metadata from a different executable revision, use focus/skip mode as release evidence, or label bounded Kani evidence as unbounded. The evidence gate (ADR-0009) rejects these as binding-stale, run-focused or outcome-skipped, and admits partial-bounds evidence only at bounded.
bets.falsifier: Consumers depend on private IR layout, relevant source changes do not invalidate evidence, or proof CI exceeds agreed limits without an explicit scope decision.
bets.decision_rule: Refine the public lemma surface, cache keys and verification profiles; no compatibility shim is required for obsolete unreleased APIs, but released proof contracts get deliberate versioning.
bets.measurement: Record workload, compiler/verifier/backend revisions, target/features, assumptions, and cost against the pre-registered acceptance controls (spec/acceptance-controls.json). Correctness gates are categorical; empirical thresholds are the registered controls.
